summary: Python library that explains machine learning predictions with Shapley values, showing how much each feature pushed a prediction up or down.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) uses game theory to explain the output of any machine learning model. It assigns each input feature a contribution to a prediction, and offers fast exact algorithms for tree models (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, scikit-learn, PySpark), explainers for deep learning (TensorFlow, Keras, PyTorch) and transformers, a model-agnostic KernelExplainer, and plots to visualize the results.
sixtySeconds.problem: Complex models are black boxes. SHAP shows why a model made a prediction, which helps with debugging, trust and reporting.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a widely used, theory-based method with explainers for almost every model type and clear plots.
requirements: The ML library of the model you want to explain

overview: Install from PyPI or conda-forge. GPU support is described in the README.
For a tree model, create shap.Explainer(model), compute shap_values = explainer(X), then plot, for example a waterfall plot for one prediction. The same syntax works for many model types.
There are sample notebooks for each explainer and documentation notebooks. It is MIT licensed.
